blocks.text: אַתָּה זוֹכֵר מַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם וּפוֹקֵד כָּל־יְצֽוּרֵי קֶֽדֶם. לְפָנֶֽיךָ נִגְלוּ כָּל־תַּעֲלֻמוֹת וַהֲמוֹן נִסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁמִּבְּרֵאשִׁית. כִּי אֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶֽךָ. וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מִנֶּֽגֶד עֵינֶֽיךָ: אַתָּה זוֹכֵר אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּפְעָל. וְגַם כָּל־הַיְצוּר לֹא נִכְחָד מִמֶּֽךָּ. הַכֹּל גָּלוּי וְיָדֽוּעַ לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ. צוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט עַד סוֹף כָּל־הַדּוֹרוֹת. כִּי תָבִיא חֹק זִכָּרוֹן לְהִפָּקֵד כָּל־רֽוּחַ וָנָֽפֶשׁ. לְהִזָּכֵר מַעֲשִׂים רַבִּים וַהֲמוֹן בְּרִיּוֹת לְאֵין תַּכְלִית. מֵרֵאשִׁית כָּזֹאת הוֹדָֽעְתָּ. וּמִלְּפָנִים אוֹתָהּ גִּלִּֽיתָ. זֶה הַיּוֹם תְּחִלַּת מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ זִכָּרוֹן לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן. כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב: וְעַל הַמְּדִינוֹת בּוֹ יֵאָמֵר אֵיזוֹ לַחֶֽרֶב. וְאֵיזוֹ לַשָּׁלוֹם. אֵיזוֹ לָרָעָב. וְאֵיזוֹ לַשּֽׂבַע. וּבְרִיּוֹת בּוֹ יִפָּקֵֽדוּ. לְהַזְכִּירָם לַחַיִּים וְלַמָּֽוֶת: מִי לֹא נִפְקַד כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה. כִּי זֵֽכֶר כָּל הַיְצוּר לְפָנֶֽיךָ בָּא. מַעֲשֵׂה אִישׁ וּפְקֻדָּתוֹ. וַעֲלִילוֹת מִצְעֲדֵי גָֽבֶר. מַחְשְׁבוֹת אָדָם וְתַחְבּוּלוֹתָיו וְיִצְרֵי מַעַלְלֵי אִישׁ: אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכָּחֶֽךָּ. וּבֶן־אָדָם יִתְאַמֶּץ־בָּךְ. כִּי דוֹרְשֶֽׁיךָ לְעוֹלָם לֹא יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ. וְלֹא יִכָּלְמוּ לָנֶֽצַח כָּל־הַחוֹסִים בָּךְ: כִּי זֵֽכֶר כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים לְפָנֶֽיךָ בָא וְאַתָּה דוֹרֵשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה כֻלָּם:

blocks.text: אַן װאָכענטאַג װירד היער גלײך מיט זכר ת״ו בעגאָננען; אַם שַׁבָּת בעטעט מאַן אַבער ערזט פאָלגענדעז: אונד דאַנן אֶפְחַד ת״ו.
uncertainties: The abbreviation after זכר and after אפחד looks like ת״ו. It could also be ת״כ or ת״ז. Its meaning is unclear (possibly 'etc.').
The first words are read as אַן װאָכענטאַג; it could instead be װאָכענטאַגען.
The final word before the colon could be פאָלגענדעז or פאָלגענדע followed by a colon.
The Rashi-script alef resembles het/mem, so אונד is printed in a form that looks like חוכד. I normalized nothing beyond reading it as אונד.
Meaning: weekdays go straight to זכר; on Shabbat the following (וגם את נח) is said first, then אפחד. This governs the placement of the weekday/Shabbat blocks below the rule on s278–s280.

blocks.text: Thou rememberest the work of the world and Thou art aware of all creatures of antiquity. Before Thee all secrets are revealed and the multitude of hidden things from the beginning of time. There is no forgetfulness before Thy glorious throne and there is nought concealed before Thine eyes. Thou rememberest every deed and not even one creature is hidden from Thee. Everything is exposed and known before Thee, O Lord our God, watching and looking to the end of all generations. For Thou dost bring a fixed time for remembrance, when every spirit and soul will be considered and many deeds and an infinite mass of creatures will be remembered. From the beginning hast Thou made this known and long ago revealed it. This is the day of the beginning of Thy works, a memorial of the first day, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob. And regarding territories, it is decided on it which shall be for the sword and which for peace, which for famine and which for plenty. And the creatures will be considered on it to be mentioned either for life or death. Who is not considered on this day? Indeed the memory of every created thing comes before Thee, man's work and his task, the actions of man's footsteps, man's thought and his devices, and the motives of man's deeds. Fortunate the man who does not forget Thee and the son of man who clings to Thee, for those that seek Thee will never stumble nor will those that take refuge with Thee ever be disgraced. For the remembrance of all actions comes before Thee and Thou dost examine all of them.
uncertainties: I removed line-wrap hyphens in glori-ous, remem-brance, remem-bered.
Italic.

blocks.text: Noah also didst Thou remember in love and consider for the sake of salvation and compassion when Thou didst bring the waters of the flood to destroy all flesh because of the wickedness of their actions. Therefore his memory came before Thee, O Lord our God, to increase his descendants like the dust of the earth and his offspring like the sand of the sea.

blocks.text: זֵֽכֶר תְּחִלַּת כָּל מַעַשׂ. אֲשֶׁר בְּכָל שָׁנָה נַעַשׂ. תּוֹחַלְתָּם לְמָאַס. יוֹצֵר כֹּל יִזְכּוֹר: תּוֹכַחַת מַעַשׂ. אִם יָצְאָה בְּכַעַס. תּוֹמֵךְ לְמַעֲנוֹ יַעַשׂ. וִיצוּרִים יִזְכּוֹר: זֵֽכֶר שֶׁמִּבְּרֵאשִׁית. תְּבוּאַת רֵאשִׁית. שֹֽׁרֶשׁ בִּכּוּר רֵאשִׁית. יֵרֶא וְיִזְכּוֹר: שֶֽׁצֶף חֲרִישִׁית. אִם חָר לְהָשִׁית. שׁוּבָה אֲשֶׁר הֵשִׁית. לַשּׁוֹבָבִים יִזְכֹּר: זֵֽכֶר רֹאשׁ עֲפָרוֹת. וְתוֹלְדוֹת סְפוּרוֹת. רְשׁוּם סְפוּרוֹת. לְמִסְפַּר חוֹל יִזְכּוֹר: רֶֽבַע מִסְפָּרוֹת. מְחַנְנֵי לְכַפָּרוֹת. רֶֽגֶשׁ שׁוֹפָרוֹת. לְשַׁפְּרֵם יִזְכּוֹר: זֵֽכֶר קְרִיאַת סֵפֶר. אֲשֶׁר גָּלְמִי שִׁפֵּר. קָצַב לוֹ בַּסֵּפֶר. בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר לִזְכּוֹר: קֶֽצֶב אִם

blocks.text: אֶפְחַד בְּמַעֲשַׂי. אֶדְאַג בְּכָל עֵת. אִירָא בְּיוֹם דִּין. בְּבוֹאִי לְזִכָּרוֹן: אֶדְרוֹשׁ לְחַנּוּן. אֲחַלֶּה לְרַחוּם. אֲחַנֵּן לְחַק לִי. יוֹם לְזִכָּרוֹן: בְּבוֹאִי לְמִשְׁפָּט. בְּמִי אֶשָּׁעֵן. וּמִי יְחַפֶּשׂ לִי. צֶֽדֶק לְזִכָּרוֹן: בָּאָבוֹת בָּטַֽחְתִּי. וּפָעֳלָם אָכַֽלְתִּי. וְהֵם הָיוּ לִי. קֶֽדֶם לְזִכָּרוֹן: גָּבְרָה זְרוֹעִי. כְּשָׁח מְחֵנִי נָא. לְבַל יִמַּח מֶֽנִּי. שֵׁם וְזִכָּרוֹן: גֶּֽבֶר אִם יַעֲמוֹד לְפָנָיו הֲיוֹעִיל. בְּעֵת יְבֻקַּשׁ מֶֽנִּי. זְכוּת לְזִכָּרוֹן: דַּצְתִּי בְּלוֹבֵשׁ אֵפוֹד. וְחֹֽשֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּט. אֲשֶׁר בָּם הוּחַק. שְׁמִי לְזִכָּרוֹן: דִּלֵּג בְּמַחְתָּה. עַד יֵעָצֵר נֶֽגֶף. בְּגֶֽשֶׁת זָר מְכַהֵן. יָקוּד לְזִכָּרוֹן: הַבִּֽיטָה אֵל. בְּעָמְדִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ. אֵין בְּקִרְבִּי אֱנוֹשׁ. תָּוִי לְזִכָּרוֹן: הֲיֵשׁ מִי יְפַלֵּל. וְיָשִׁיב

blocks.text: On the day of memory of the beginning of all action, let the Creator not remember those of the deeds of the whole year that are in conflict with Israel's hopes. If reproof for those deeds has gone forth in anger, may He grant help for His own sake and remember the creatures. May He look and recall the memory of the people He first appointed, the first harvest, the root of the first fruit. When in His anger He determines to send severe punishment, may He remember the atonement which He has ordained for the faithless. He remembers the first man who was formed from dust, the countless generations and the inscribed (good deeds) on behalf of the people that is like the sand in number. He remembers those counted in four camps who implore expiation and sound the Shofar in order to purify themselves. He remembers what was read out from the book that was bestowed by Him upon the first man even before its completion. He had decided in that book that He was to be remembered in every generation. blocks.text: I am anxious because of my deeds, I worry constantly, I fear on the day of judgment, when I come for remembrance. I seek out the Merciful, I entreat the Compassionate, I implore Him who has appointed this day for me for remembrance. When I come in judgment, on whom shall I rely, who will find righteousness for me as a remembrance? Upon the fathers I put my trust, I derive benefit from their work, they have from of old served as my remembrance. My arm was strong when Moses pleaded to be wiped out, so that my name should not be wiped out nor should my remembrance. Should a man stand before the Lord, can he then help me, when merit is required from me for remembrance. I rejoiced with him (Aaron) who wore the Ephod and the Breast-plate of Judgment on which my name was engraved for remembrance. He hastened with his censor until the plague had abated, when a stranger (Korah) approached to act as priest, the flames devoured him as a remembrance. הֶחֱרַט בַּסֵּֽפֶר. לְבִלְתִּי מְצוֹא כֹּֽפֶר. קִיּוּם זִכְרוֹן זֶה סֵֽפֶר. לְפָנָיו יִזְכּוֹר: זֵֽכֶר צָפוּן מֹרְדֵי אוֹר. תָּמִים דּוֹר כָּאוֹר. צִיָּה כְּחָר לָאוֹר. קְנוּיָו יִזְכֹּר: צְפוּפִים פְּנֵי נָאוֹר. מִשְׁפָּטָם תֵּת לָאוֹר. צַחַן רֹֽעַ שְׂאוֹר. בְּרִיב בַּל יִזְכּוֹר: זֵֽכֶר פְּעֻלַּת אֶזְרָח. הֵעַרְתָּהוּ מִמִּזְרָח. פָּעֳלוֹ יִזְרָח. בְּקֶֽרֶב שָׁנִים יִזְכֹּר: פַּח אִם הֻטְרַח. פִּרְחָיו לִמְרַח. פִּלּוּלוֹ יִצְרַח. בַּעֲדָם יִזְכּוֹר: זֵֽכֶר עֲקֵדַת מוֹרִיָּה. כְּהִיַּת רְאִיָּה. עֲדֵי עָרוֹם וְעֶרְיָה. סְבוּכוֹ יִזְכּוֹר: עֵֽצֶב טְרִיָּה. אִם כּוֹאֲבָה פּוֹרִיָּה. עֲתָרוֹ לִרְאִיָּה. וְלִזְכוּת יִזְכֹּר: זֵֽכֶר סֻלָּם חֲלָם. וְעָלָיו מְחוֹלְלָם. שָׂרֵי אַרְבַּע וְעֻלָּם. כּוֹ. כְּמֵאָז יִזְכֹּר: שְׂרִיגָיו בְּמַעֲלָם. וַיֹּאמַר לְנַעֲלָם. שִׂיחוֹ

He remembers the hidden one (Noah) in the age of open rebels, the perfect and the pure; when He is angry and wishes to curse the earth, He remembers those acquired by Him (Israel). As to those who stand crowded together before the countenance of the Awe-inspiring, may He bring to light their judgment; may He not in strife recall the ugly evil leaven. He remembers the work of that strong one whom He told to rise up from the east (Abraham). May He soon recall his shining act. When destruction threatens to annihilate his offspring, may his supplication become audible that He may remember them kindly. He remembers the sacrifice on Moriah (Isaac) whose eyes become dim; for the sake of people naked and bare, may He recall the ram caught in the thicket. When the fruitful people is afflicted with a festering wound, may his prayer be manifest that God may remember his merit. He remembers him who saw the ladder in the dream (Jacob); above it the Creator appeared to him, showed him the princes of the four empires and their yoke. He will remember him, as in former days. Who is it that hates gain that he might say: “Testify against me”, and the Lord Himself replied as a witness for remembrance. With a sucking lamb he (Samuel) atoned for us and, equal to the noble pair of brothers (Moses and Aaron), he rises for remembrance. When he saw the wrath of the Lord, he (David) said: “Let Thy hand turn against me”, that he conformed to the will of his God is his remembrance. He cried out and caused the angel's sword to return to its sheath, therefore was his throne established as firmly as the sun for remembrance. At the time of drought I wait for Him who releases and brings rain (Elijah), who restored breath to the child already lost to remembrance. He lives on as a witness at circumcisions because he spoke of his zeal when the people had abandoned both covenant and remembrance. Formerly I had one who could atone before the Lord, when he brought the meal-offering as a bribe for remembrance. Gifts of nard and spices perfumed His chambers, blood and fat as a delight and the show-bread for remembrance. I was placed like an empty vessel upon the coals, that Israel may not be widowed, I plead
